purpose: Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as ear infections, throat infections (like strep throat), urinary tract infections, and certain sexually transmitted infections like gonorrhea. It works only against bacteria, so it will not help with viral infections like the common cold or flu. Your doctor prescribed it because you have a specific bacterial infection that this medicine can fight.
how_it_works: Cefixime works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria, which bacteria need to survive. It basically pokes holes in that wall, causing the bacteria to fall apart and die. Over the course of your treatment, it clears the infection by destroying the harmful bacteria in your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, loose stools, stomach pain, nausea, and gas. Some people may also experience headaches or mild skin rash. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own as your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin or any other antibiotics, as you may also be allergic to cefixime. Do not stop taking it early even if you feel better, because stopping too soon can let the infection come back or cause antibiotic resistance. Contact your doctor right away if you develop severe diarrhea, a severe skin rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, as these could be signs of a serious reaction. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have kidney problems.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 400 mg taken once a day, or 200 mg taken twice a day, for 7 to 14 days depending on the infection. For children, the dose is based on body weight and is determined by the doctor. Always take the full course of antibiotics as prescribed, even if you start feeling better after a few days.
